$comment: THE-751: permission overlay for the public evergreen (Matuschak) corpus, so retrieval can be
evaluated per-principal under a REAL FolderAcl. The overlay is ARBITRARY; the ground truth it
implies is NOT — expected_P = expected INTERSECT {p : readableRel(A, p)} is computed, never
judged. Say both wherever a number from this is published.
PARTITION: alphabetical by note-title first character, 4 principals, ranges deliberately
OVERLAPPING at the seams. Overlap is the one design choice copied directly from the RBAC
text-to-SQL paper (arXiv 2607.22115): with disjoint roles any out-of-whitelist path is
trivially detectable and the leakage test proves nothing.
Measured against the 78-query golden sets before committing to it:
union coverage           77/78 strict, 78/78 lenient  (no query orphaned)
scoreable for >1         41/78 strict, 69/78 lenient  (the overlap that matters)
WHY LITERAL PREFIX GLOBS RATHER THAN [a-f]: measured 2026-08-08 against FolderAcl —
character classes ('notes/[a-f]*') and braces ('notes/{a,b}*') do NOT match. Only literal
prefixes do. AND GLOBS ARE CASE-SENSITIVE: 'notes/a*' does not match 'notes/Attention.md'.
So every letter needs BOTH cases, which is why these lists are ~2x longer than the ticket
estimated. Digits are in P4 because 194 of 1,357 notes begin with '2' (dated titles) — by far
the largest single bucket, and it would unbalance any principal it landed in silently.
